manojit saha Mumbai, 4 November The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has formed a Technical Consult- ative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM), headed by deputy governor in-charge of Financial Markets Regulation Department, currently Rohit Jain, against the backdrop of rapidly evolving ﬁnancial markets and infrastructure. The panel, which will have seven external members, will meet at least once in a quarter. “The committee will serve as a forum for structured engagement with market participants and stakeholders by the Reserve Bank on policy and operational matters related to money, government securities and foreign exchange markets as well as the respective derivative markets and infrastruc- ture,” RBI said in a press release. The central bank had said such a committee will be formed during the October review of monetary policy, details of which were announced on Tuesday. The committee is formed at a time when there is volatility in the ﬁnancial markets, mainly due to the geopolitical conﬂicts, resulting in elevated energy prices. There have been relentless outﬂows of foreign investors from equity mar- kets in the past two years though there have been some inﬂows in the past few days. Foreign exchanges reserves, on the other hand, fell $66 billion in the past seven weeks after hitting fresh high of $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4, 2026, as the central bank sold dollars in the foreign exchange market to curb volatility. Against this backdrop, the central bank has kick started a rate hike cycle last month, and wants to ensure transmission of monetary policy rates. In the past, there has been a technical advisory committee on monetary policy, which was dis- continued after the ﬂexible inﬂa- tion targeting regime was operationalised in October 2016 with the six-member monetary policy committee. Market participants said the central bank has been consulting with market participants over the years, now such deliberations have been formalised. “The members will provide market feedback to the regulator, may be on products, what measures can be taken when there is untoward volatility,” said a market participant. The members cover a wide spectrum of the ﬁnancial sectors, which includes public sector, pri- vate sector and foreign banks, treasury experts and equity market specialists, and experts having experience in regulatory bodies. The terms of reference include issues related to the func- tioning, efficiency, liquidity and resilience of the money, govern- ment securities, foreign exchange and related derivative markets, and identiﬁcation of measures to deepen and broaden these mar- kets. “There is always a trade-off between ﬁnancial market devel- opment and macroeconomic dynamics. The committee should look at ways to balance the two,” said a ﬁnancial market expert. The panel will also look at emerging policy and operational issues affecting ﬁnancial markets, including implementation of RBI measures and identiﬁcation of unintended market frictions. “RBI may take some steps on liquidity but it may have implica- tions of other markets. Under- standing those dynamics are also important,” said another market participant. One of the term of ref- erence is to address issues relating to trading, clearing, settlement, reporting and other market infra- structure, including the associ- ated regulatory and operational frameworks. RBI forms panel for consultation on ﬁnancial mkts Financial experts External members of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM) The committee will be by chaired by the Deputy Governor (DG) in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department (FMRD) of the Reserve Bank of India Ananth Narayan Former Whole-time member, Sebi, and Professor of Practice, IIT Bombay Shamsher Singh Chairman, Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India (FIMMDA) and deputy managing director, State Bank of India Neeraj Gambhir Executive director, Axis Bank Shailendra Jhingan Head, Treasury and Economic Research, ICICI Bank Aditya Bagree Managing director, head (Markets), Citibank India; Nand Kishore Managing director, Clearing Corporation of India Limited; and Ridham Desai Managing director, Morgan Stanley India
